description: Deterministic marker-based GC for scripts/cam/patterns.md mirroring the journal-archive on-main plumbing, so the hot file stays scannable while living invariants are preserved.

userStories.title: archivePatternsOnMain core logic (marker-based, on-main commit-tree)
userStories.description: As a cam maintainer, I need a deterministic function that moves only resolved-marked bullets from patterns.md to patterns.archive.md on main, so the hot file stays scannable without losing living invariants or history.
acceptanceCriteria: A new src/commands/patterns-archive.ts exports archivePatternsOnMain, reusing the SHARED on-main plumbing (checkMainUpToDate, commitTreeToMain, pushMainBestEffort from src/git/on-main.ts), never a private copy and never a working-tree commit path. [oracle: grep -q 'commitTreeToMain' src/commands/patterns-archive.ts]

Only bullets carrying an explicit resolved marker (a leading resolved tag, e.g. `[resolved YYYY-MM]`, recognized by the parser) are moved from scripts/cam/patterns.md to scripts/cam/patterns.archive.md; unmarked bullets (living invariants) and the file's intro preamble are always retained. [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts]

The selection criterion is NOT position/age/count based: an old-but-unmarked bullet is retained; the journal-archive 'oldest third' criterion is NOT reused (only its commit-tree plumbing is). [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts]

scripts/cam/patterns.archive.md is lazily created: absent-on-main is treated as empty and bootstrapped with a minimal header, matching journal.archive.md behavior (never an error). [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts]

Marked and remaining content land in ONE atomic on-main commit via commitTreeToMain (read via `git show main:<path>`, working branch untouched); push to origin main is best-effort. [oracle: grep -q 'pushMainBestEffort' src/commands/patterns-archive.ts]
A run with no marked bullets is a clean no-op (returns ok:true with archived:0, emits no commit). [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts]
Guards return typed errors when patterns.md is missing on main or main is diverged/detached (mirroring archiveJournalOnMain's guard order). [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Model the new file on src/commands/journal-archive.ts (archiveJournalOnMain, line ~209): same guard order (checkMainUpToDate -> read-from-main -> parse -> mutate), same 2-element FileWrite[] atomic commitTreeToMain, same lazy-archive read (readArchiveFromMain returns null when absent). Shared exports live in src/git/on-main.ts (checkMainUpToDate, commitTreeToMain, pushMainBestEffort, FileWrite, SpawnFn) - import them, do not copy. GOTCHA (issue): the 'oldest third' selection does NOT transfer; patterns bullets are append-only invariants where old != stale. Reuse the PLUMBING, not the criterion. patterns.md bullets are line-level `- ` entries (not `## ` headers like journal); parse everything before the first top-level `- ` as preamble to preserve, then classify each `- ` bullet by whether it carries the resolved marker. Decide the marker regex here (parser is authoritative; US-004 retrofits + documents to match). patterns.md must pre-exist on main (guard 'patterns-missing'). noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard all array/regex-group access. Test template: test/commands/journal-archive.test.ts (inject a fake SpawnFn, no real git).

userStories.title: cam patterns archive CLI wiring + help + sentinel
userStories.description: As an operator, I need `cam patterns archive` to invoke archivePatternsOnMain and print a machine-readable sentinel, so I can archive resolved bullets manually and see the outcome.
acceptanceCriteria: index.ts dispatches a new `patterns archive` subcommand that calls archivePatternsOnMain; it takes NO --threshold flag (archival is marker-based, not count-based). [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-cli.test.ts]

On a successful archive the command prints a sentinel `CAM_PATTERNS_ARCHIVED=<n> sha=<sha>`; on a no-marked-bullets run it prints `CAM_PATTERNS_ARCHIVE=noop` and exits 0; on an error it returns exit 1 (mirroring the journal-archive dispatch shape). [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-cli.test.ts]
`cam patterns --help` / `cam patterns` (no subcommand) print usage/help registered alongside the existing help entries. [oracle: grep -q 'patterns archive' index.ts]

The dispatch function accepts injectable deps (archiveFn, writeStdout) so tests verify sentinel emission and exit codes without touching real git or stdout. [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-cli.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Mirror the journal wiring in index.ts: parseJournalArgs (~line 1324), dispatchJournal (~1435), JournalDispatchDeps (injectable archiveFn/writeStdout), defaultArchiveFn (~1416), and the JOURNAL help/usage blocks (~355-427). Add an equivalent patterns block. Single-hub dispatch invariant (patterns.md 'Single-hub dispatch invariant'): `cam` subcommands are thin-proxies; verify whether `cam patterns archive` should run inline (like `cam journal archive`, which does) - journal archive dispatches directly, so patterns archive should too. NO --threshold arg (marker-based). Keep the sentinel-emission pattern (writeStdout injectable). Test template: test/commands/journal-archive.test.ts plus the index.ts dispatch tests.

userStories.title: Best-effort patterns archive on the --cycle-close path
userStories.description: As the cam sidecar, I need patterns archive to run best-effort at cycle close alongside journal archive, so resolved bullets are swept automatically without ever blocking handoff.
acceptanceCriteria: On the --cycle-close path in dispatchJournal (index.ts), patterns archive is invoked best-effort alongside the existing journal-archive check, strictly BEFORE the recycle marker is armed and CAM_ORCH_HANDOFF_DUE is emitted. [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-cli.test.ts]

The patterns-archive invocation is best-effort: an ok:false result or a thrown error logs a warning only and never changes dispatchJournal's exit code, never blocks marker arming or handoff (mirroring the journal-archive best-effort block). [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-cli.test.ts]

A manual `cam patterns archive` invocation (US-002) still works unchanged; plain `cam journal append` without --cycle-close never triggers the patterns archive. [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-cli.test.ts]
The patterns-archive fn is injectable via JournalDispatchDeps so the cycle-close test asserts it is called and that a failure is swallowed. [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-cli.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: The --cycle-close best-effort block lives in dispatchJournal (index.ts ~1505-1548), inside `if (parsed.cycleClose)`, AFTER the handoff-exists (exit 3) and watcher-alive (exit 4) guards, AFTER the journal-archive try/catch, and BEFORE armMarker(). Add the patterns-archive call in the same try/catch style (printWarning on ok:false or throw, then continue). GOTCHA: once the marker is armed the watcher can SIGTERM this process, so keep the patterns archive strictly before armMarker. Add a patternsArchiveFn dep to JournalDispatchDeps + a default wired to the real archivePatternsOnMain with process.cwd() and a real spawnSync (mirror defaultArchiveFn). This story edits index.ts (same file as US-002) - sequenced after it.

userStories.title: Retrofit 2026-06 build-notes markers + document marking convention
userStories.description: As a cam maintainer, I need the already-identified one-time 2026-06 build-notes marked resolved and the marking convention documented, so the first archive run has real content to move and future authors know how to mark bullets.
acceptanceCriteria: The already-identified one-time 2026-06 build-notes in scripts/cam/patterns.md (ink-testing-library keypress/setState/chalk/ESC timing bullets and the tmux window-resized resize-pane arithmetic bullet) are retrofitted with the resolved marker whose format matches the US-001 parser; living invariants are left unmarked. [oracle: grep -qE '^- \[resolved 2026-06\]' scripts/cam/patterns.md]

The marking convention (what the resolved marker looks like and that `cam patterns archive` moves marked bullets to patterns.archive.md) is documented in the Knowledge-Layer Routing section of scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md. [oracle: grep -q 'patterns.archive.md' scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md]

The same documentation change is applied to BOTH copies (scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md and templates/scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md) and re-embedded via bun run embed-vendor. [oracle: grep -q 'patterns.archive.md' templates/scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md]
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check). [oracle: bun run embed-vendor:check]

A test (or the US-001 parser applied to the real patterns.md fixture) confirms the retrofitted bullets are recognized as marked and would be the ones moved. [oracle: bun test test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Lint/static spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Retrofit targets (issue names them): the ink-testing-library bullets ('ink-testing-library keypress simulation', 'ink-testing-library setState re-render timing', 'chalk.level and ANSI in ink-testing-library', 'Ink 7 ESC pending-buffer') and 'tmux window-resized hook + resize-pane -x clamp' - all one-time 2026-06 build-notes documenting resolved mechanics, not living invariants. Do NOT mark durable invariants (Bun runtime, permission-mode, claude -p forbidden, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, Ink success/failure glyph, single-hub dispatch, sidecar-supervisor). Marker format must match the US-001 parser exactly. Document in scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md 'Knowledge-Layer Routing' section (the patterns.md row / routing notes), BOTH copies, then `bun run embed-vendor` to regen src/vendor/_generated.ts. GOTCHA (issue): patterns.md is grep-on-demand since CAM-223 (shipped); this mechanism is for file hygiene/scannability, NOT context reduction - do not reintroduce a full-read. Location convention: patterns.md and patterns.archive.md stay under scripts/cam/, do not relocate. CAM-224 (shared CLAUDE.md editor) is already shipped, so no concurrent-edit risk.
